title: Descriptions, definitions, and a short history of turbulence
status: reviewed and locally validated; passes 1-9 complete; gate 6b passed round 2 (0 blocking)
transcript_provenance: Local machine transcription (faster-whisper small.en); not publisher captions
source_uncertainties: The lecture's 'modern definition' of turbulence is attributed on the slide only through the lead-in 'Chapman and Tobak (1985) have described ... three eras ... A more precise definition is now possible within the context of ideas from the deterministic era'. The defining sentence is not in NASA TM 86679 (searched for 'chaotic solution', 'sensitive to initial', 'successive instabilit', 'bifurcation parameter', 'definition'). Its source was not found; McDonough (2007) and Bakker (2008), named on Module 01's Sources slide per chapter 1, were not obtained.

Not obtained, so given 'as stated in the lecture': Hinze (1959), von Kármán (1938) quoting Taylor, Tsinober (2001), Tennekes and Lumley (1972), Taylor (1935) and (1938), Prandtl (1925), Ruelle and Takens (1971; Project Euclid landing page only, PDF text not accessible), Landau (1944), the Kolmogorov 1941 papers other than the one translation in chapter 5, and all names of the 1940s-1990s entries on the timeline slide.

Reynolds's constants B_s=43.79 (p. 943), B_c=278 (p. 948; 279.7 and 272.0 in tubes 4 and 5, pp. 970-971) and A_c=47,700,000 (pp. 948, 972) were read from the extracted text and, for p. 948, from the page image (the ratio 43.7 on p. 948 is Reynolds's rounding of 43.79); the identification of Reynolds's i with head loss per unit length and g=9.81 m/s^2 are assumptions of the conversion (nu(0 C)=1.787e-6 m^2/s, Re_c=2.01e3, Re_s=1.28e4). The tube diameters near 1, 1/2 and 1/4 inch on p. 941 are partly illegible in the extracted text; the chapter computes with 12.7 mm as an illustrative value, and Re does not depend on D.

Source of the modern definition: the slide quotes the sentence and names no source; the lecturer says (L5, 975-980 s) that the modern definition of turbulence sort of came from the Ruelle and Takens paper, which was not accessible. Water viscosity at 0 C (1.7921 mPa s, density 0.99984 g/cm3, Lide 2004, p. 6-201) is quoted as cited by the Wikipedia data page for water; the handbook was not opened.
Reynolds 1894/1895: Darrigol (2002) cites 'Reynolds [1894]' (Phil. Trans. (1894)); Schmitt (2007) cites 1895. The paper was not opened; the chapter states both dates.

Lecture-stated values not verified: Re < 2300 / 2300-10000 / > 10000 (handwritten); cylinder wake: the lecture's 'quasi-periodic above 150' and 'fully turbulent at 5000-10000' disagree with Roshko and with Chapman and Tobak (its steady Re about 10 and periodic 50-150 agree); 'almost 300 years later' for 1877 (slide: > 100 yrs, actual about 150); Boussinesq 'himself offered a warning' (slide: 'Warning offered about the relationship', no author); chaotic solutions of 1-D and 2-D Navier-Stokes equations (no source found; chapter notes that 1-D incompressible flow has no spatial dynamics); 'RANS makes little sense if turbulence is random' (not in the text of Chapman and Tobak read).

Corrsin and Kistler (1955) page numbers use report page = PDF page - 3 (INDEX.md): definition of the intermittency factor PDF p. 8 = p. 5; Figure 32 PDF p. 28 = p. 25. Chapman and Tobak page numbers are the memorandum's own: PDF page - 2. Schmitt page numbers are preprint pages: PDF page - 1.

ASR spellings in the recordings (not used in reader text): 'Heinz' for Hinze, 'Bornkam' for von Karman, 'business', 'Bismiss' and 'Bissonin' for Boussinesq, 'Rolle and Teckens' for Ruelle and Takens, 'Laundry' for Launder, 'Figgen-Gau' for Feigenbaum, 'Lazure and Matras' for Lesieur and Metais, 'co-ep' for Couette, 'walls/vaults' for whirls, 'errors' for eras; the speaker says 'Chapman and Tobach 1981' (L5 about 1212 s) where the slide and the report give 1985; L5 places Reynolds's pipe experiments at 1894 (slide date of his seminal paper; the experiments are of 1883).
